headline: Amazon replaces Fire Tablets with new Alexa Tablets
summary: Amazon unveiled three new Alexa Tablets (12 Pro, 11 and 8) that run Android with full Google Play access, replacing the Fire Tablet brand and OS. The lineup includes kids' versions, and the 12 Pro starts at about $500.

claims.statement: Amazon unveiled three new Alexa Tablet models: the 12 Pro, 11 and 8.

sources.quote: The lineup includes three models: Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.

claims.statement: The new tablets run Android with full access to the Google Play Store, replacing Fire OS.

sources.quote: The three new aluminum Alexa Tablets now run Android with full access to the Google Play Store. There are versions for kids too.
Amazon's new Alexa tablets will have full access to Google Play

claims.statement: Amazon is phasing out the Fire Tablet brand in favor of Alexa Tablets.

sources.quote: Amazon is phasing out Fire Tablets because they weren’t ‘giving customers what they were asking for’
Amazon's new Alexa Tablets drop the Fire branding but are more Android than ever

claims.statement: The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at about $500.

sources.quote: It's a promising tablet that starts at about $500.

claims.statement: Amazon is also releasing kids' versions of the new tablets, available in two sizes.

sources.quote: Amazon is releasing kids' versions of its new Alexa Tablets
The new Amazon Kids Tablets come in two sizes and can be bundled with one of two styles of case.

claims.statement: The 12-inch model includes an anti-glare screen.

sources.quote: Amazon's new Alexa tablets include a 12-inch model with anti-glare screen

claims.statement: Reviewers compared the 12 Pro's nanomatte screen and Kindle mode favorably to Amazon's own Fire HD 10 and to Apple's iPad Pro.

sources.quote: Amazon's best tablet ever didn't have to work hard for the title, but a new nanomatte screen and Kindle mode sweeten the deal.
Amazon's latest and greatest tablet shares some key similarities to Apple's high-end iPads, but the devil is in the details.
